Compared with the photometric approach, it is over 20 times faster, matches rendering quality, and improves surface accuracy, reducing the chamfer distance of the Delaunay mesh on Replica from 1.55 to 0.86 cm. We will release the implementation at this https URL.

AI.tldr: Facet-SLAM is a real-time RGB-D triangle splatting SLAM system that separates geometric GICP tracking from non-translating map optimization, running at ~100 FPS and halving Replica mesh chamfer distance from 1.55 to 0.86 cm.
AI.motivation: 3D Gaussian splatting SLAM produces poor surface geometry, while triangle splatting SLAM has relied on slow photometric tracking that cannot run at sensor rate, and naive geometric registration fails when mapping displaces triangles.
AI.method: Facet-SLAM sets triangle centroids from fused depth for GICP tracking while restricting the mapper to non-translating updates via a change of variables, preserving reliable geometric registration targets.
AI.result: Facet-SLAM achieves competitive tracking at ~100 FPS on a desktop GPU and sensor rate on a Jetson AGX Orin—over 20x faster than photometric triangle splatting—while matching rendering quality and reducing Replica Delaunay mesh chamfer distance from 1.55 to 0.86 cm.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling depth-anchored GICP tracking from non-translating triangle optimization enables real-time, mesh-ready dense SLAM.

title: WAM-Policy: World Action Models with On-Policy Distillation for Quadrupedal Loco-Manipulation
comment: Code: this https URL, Website: this https URL
summary: Arm-free quadrupeds can perform loco-manipulation, walking on three legs while manipulating with a front leg, yet no existing policy for it follows language instructions. World action models (WAMs) have emerged as effective language-conditioned manipulation policies, but are pretrained for robot arms and sample slowly. WAM-Policy turns one WAM into a quadrupedal loco-manipulation policy via two stages. The first, Cross-Morphology Policy Adaptation and Acceleration, adapts the arm-centric WAM to quadrupeds and distills the transferred policy into a student with one video and two action steps by on-policy self-distillation (OPSD). This student, however, is bounded by its teacher, which only imitates demonstrations. The second stage, Task-Specific Improvement and Merging, therefore tunes the teacher by reinforcement learning (RL) and merges the slow specialists into one few-step student by multi-teacher on-policy distillation (M-OPD). On QLM-Bench, ten simulated tasks with 1,000 demonstrations synthesized without teleoperation, the transferred policy reaches 77.0%, and the OPSD student keeps 76.7% while sampling 14 times faster. Task-specific RL and M-OPD lift it to 85.0%. We also deploy the OPSD student on a real Unitree Go2 Air. WAM-Policy thus achieves a stronger quadrupedal policy at a fraction of the inference cost.

AI.tldr: WAM-Policy adapts arm-pretrained world action models to language-conditioned quadrupedal loco-manipulation via on-policy distillation and task-specific RL, reaching 85.0% on QLM-Bench and 14x faster sampling.
AI.motivation: No existing quadrupedal loco-manipulation policy follows language instructions, and arm-pretrained world action models (WAMs) suffer from morphology mismatch and slow sampling.
AI.method: Stage 1 adapts an arm WAM to quadrupeds and distills it into a few-step student (one video, two action steps) via on-policy self-distillation (OPSD); Stage 2 tunes specialists with RL and merges them into one student via multi-teacher on-policy distillation (M-OPD).
AI.result: On QLM-Bench (10 tasks, 1,000 demonstrations), the transferred policy reaches 77.0%, the OPSD student retains 76.7% at 14x faster sampling, and RL + M-OPD lifts performance to 85.0%; the OPSD student is also deployed on a real Unitree Go2 Air.
AI.conclusion: Cross-morphology adaptation followed by RL and multi-teacher on-policy distillation yields fast, capable language-conditioned quadrupedal loco-manipulation policies.

title: SemPhys: Semantic-Physical Co-Learning for Humanoid Motion Generation via Differentiable World Models
summary: In human-robot collaboration, natural language lets people direct a humanoid's whole-body movements without programming joint trajectories. A common approach generates a kinematic reference from an instruction and relies on a tracking controller to execute it. However, as the controller maintains balance under contact constraints, the executed motion can depart from the reference in ways that change the action it conveys. Our central insight is that semantic alignment must be evaluated directly on the complete motion the robot physically executes. Building on this insight, we introduce \textbf{SemPhys}, a framework that trains motion generators using semantic feedback from simulated executions. A differentiable world model and a fixed tracking controller predict a short segment of a recorded execution. SemPhys inserts this prediction at its original position, scores the complete trajectory against the instruction, and backpropagates through the predicted segment. A paired anchoring loss stabilizes adaptation by keeping each generated reference close to its counterpart from the initial generator. On BONES-SEED, SemPhys largely preserves instruction retrieval accuracy from reference to execution and achieves the highest retrieval accuracy on executed motions among the evaluated methods.

AI.tldr: SemPhys trains humanoid motion generators using semantic feedback from simulated physical executions rather than just kinematic references, preserving instruction alignment on BONES-SEED.
AI.motivation: Generating a kinematic reference from natural language and executing it with a tracking controller can cause the physically executed motion to deviate from the reference under balance and contact constraints, altering the conveyed action.
AI.method: SemPhys uses a differentiable world model and a fixed tracking controller to predict a short segment of a recorded execution, inserts it back into the trajectory, scores the complete motion against the instruction, and backpropagates through the predicted segment alongside a paired anchoring loss.
AI.result: On BONES-SEED, SemPhys largely preserves instruction retrieval accuracy from reference to execution and achieves the highest retrieval accuracy on executed motions among the evaluated methods.
AI.conclusion: Evaluating and backpropagating semantic alignment directly through physically executed motions prevents action drift in language-directed humanoid control.

title: Ego2X: Contact-aware Transfer from Egocentric Human Data to Any Robot
summary: Embodied models depend on real interaction data, yet collecting it on physical robots is slow and labor-intensive. Recent ego-to-robot pipelines retarget first-person view human videos to robot data via transferring hand and arm motion. They judge fidelity mainly by visual appearance. However, trajectories often fail in terms of physics: fingers hover beside objects, and grippers close on empty space. We argue that how the object moves and the contacts that drive the motion count. Thus, we present Ego2X, an object-centric framework that converts monocular egocentric video into physically executable robot data across dexterous hands and parallel grippers. Ego2X centers on CORE (Contact-centric Object-interaction REpresentation), which records each contact on the object by its surface anchor, as well as relative force, grasp mode, and interaction state. Throughout the pipeline, CORE corrects hand-object drift via object-relative constraints, steers inverse kinematics toward contacts the robot must realize, and preserves held objects during arm erasure and robot compositing. On HOT3D, contact-driven correction reduces in-contact hand depth error by 33.7%, while on EgoDex, contact-driven retargeting realizes 62.9% of annotated contacts, surpassing the official HuRo pipeline (27.9%). In RoboTwin 2.0, post-training X-VLA on Ego2X episodes alone, without simulator demonstrations, raises task success rate from 40.5% zero-shot to 67.0% across 200 paired scenes. We will publicly release our conversion pipeline and CORE-annotated dataset for dexterous hands and parallel grippers.

AI.tldr: Ego2X converts monocular egocentric human videos into physically executable robot data across dexterous hands and parallel grippers using a contact-centric object-interaction representation called CORE.
AI.motivation: Existing ego-to-robot pipelines judge retargeting fidelity mainly by visual appearance, causing trajectories to fail physically with hovering fingers or grippers closing on empty space.
AI.method: Ego2X introduces CORE, which records each object contact by surface anchor, relative force, grasp mode, and interaction state to correct hand-object drift via object-relative constraints, steer inverse kinematics toward required contacts, and preserve held objects during arm erasure and robot compositing.
AI.result: On HOT3D, contact-driven correction reduces in-contact hand depth error by 33.7%; on EgoDex, it realizes 62.9% of annotated contacts versus 27.9% for HuRo; in RoboTwin 2.0, post-training X-VLA on Ego2X episodes alone raises task success rate from 40.5% zero-shot to 67.0% across 200 paired scenes.
AI.conclusion: Centering egocentric-to-robot transfer on object-relative contact representations yields physically valid manipulation data that improves downstream robot policy learning without simulator demonstrations.

title: Efficient World-Model Planning via Physics-Guided Search Distillation
summary: World models support autonomous driving by evaluating candidate trajectories through predicted future scene evolution. However, accurate future prediction does not ensure road-compliant execution; when all candidates violate road boundaries, re-ranking cannot select a feasible trajectory. We propose Physics-Guided Search Distillation (PGSD), a single-view planning framework that combines future representations and execution feedback for verified beyond-pool repair through three components: (1) Execution-Aware Selection checks ego-vehicle road compliance under simulated execution and selects the highest-scoring feasible trajectory; (2) a Clearance-Aware Search Teacher generates beyond-pool corrections and selects demonstrations with larger minimum road-boundary clearance during execution to buffer imitation errors; and (3) a Future-Conditioned Repair Student predicts one correction from rewarder features and execution feedback for single-rollout verification. The pretrained planner and rewarder remain frozen; no future scenes are generated online. On NAVSIM v1, single-view PGSD achieves 90.97 PDMS, exceeding all compared prior single-view planners and retaining 73.2% of the search teacher's PDMS gain over execution-aware selection. On NAVSIM v2 navhard, it reaches 38.96 EPDMS, improving on WorldDrive by 11.24 points (40.5%). The student replaces up to ten search rollouts with a single verification rollout per repair trigger. HUGSIM Hard examples provide qualitative evidence of zero-shot transfer.

AI.tldr: Physics-Guided Search Distillation (PGSD) combines execution-aware trajectory selection with a future-conditioned repair student to fix road-boundary violations in single-view autonomous driving planning.
AI.motivation: Accurate future prediction in world-model planners does not guarantee road-compliant execution, and when all candidate trajectories violate road boundaries, re-ranking alone cannot produce a feasible plan.
AI.method: PGSD pairs Execution-Aware Selection under simulated execution with a Clearance-Aware Search Teacher that generates beyond-pool corrections with larger boundary clearance, and distills them into a Future-Conditioned Repair Student using frozen planner and rewarder features for single-rollout verification.
AI.result: On NAVSIM v1, single-view PGSD achieves 90.97 PDMS, surpassing all compared prior single-view planners and retaining 73.2% of the search teacher's gain; on NAVSIM v2 navhard, it reaches 38.96 EPDMS (+11.24 points or 40.5% over WorldDrive) while replacing up to ten search rollouts with one verification rollout.
AI.conclusion: Distilling physics-guided search corrections into a single-rollout repair student enables road-compliant beyond-pool planning without online future scene generation.

title: Joint Image Denoising and Interpolation via Mixed Graph Filtering
summary: Images often require both denoising and interpolation, yet treating the two tasks separately is suboptimal: interpolation introduces correlated noise that complicates subsequent denoising, while denoising may remove image details useful for interpolation. In this paper, we study joint image denoising and interpolation from a mixed graph filtering perspective, where denoising is modeled using undirected graph filters and interpolation using directed graph filters. We first establish that, under mild conditions, any (pseudo-)linear denoiser and interpolator can be interpreted as solution filters of maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation problems regularized by undirected and directed graph smoothness priors, respectively. Guided by these results, we formulate graph-based joint denoising and interpolation problems using both directed and undirected graph structures. We characterize when joint denoising/interpolation reduces to a separable pipeline and when a genuinely coupled optimization is required. For the non-separable case, we recover sparse graph operators from given denoisers and interpolators, yielding an efficient linear-system formulation solvable via conjugate gradient. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed joint framework consistently outperforms separate denoising and interpolation pipelines across multiple denoiser-interpolator combinations.

AI.tldr: This paper formulates joint image denoising and interpolation from a mixed graph filtering perspective, modeling denoising with undirected graph filters and interpolation with directed graph filters.
AI.motivation: Treating image denoising and interpolation separately is suboptimal because interpolation introduces correlated noise that complicates denoising, whereas denoising can erase details needed for interpolation.
AI.method: The authors interpret (pseudo-)linear denoisers and interpolators as MAP estimators with undirected and directed graph smoothness priors, characterize when the joint problem is separable versus coupled, and recover sparse graph operators for non-separable cases to solve a linear system via conjugate gradient.
AI.result: Experiments show that the proposed joint framework consistently outperforms separate denoising and interpolation pipelines across multiple denoiser-interpolator combinations.
AI.conclusion: Unifying undirected and directed graph smoothness priors provides a principled, efficient linear-system formulation for coupled image denoising and interpolation.

title: Transferable Named Sparse Features for Morphology-based Gleason Grading
summary: Deep learning systems grade prostate biopsies at the level of pathologists, but most report a grade without the glandular architecture that justifies it. This work presents a grading system built on a sparse code over the tokens of a pathology foundation model. A sparse autoencoder pretrained on biopsies is aligned with multi-reader annotations, so that 69 of its 2048 features are named after Gleason morphologies such as cribriform glands, cords, and comedonecrosis. The same code feeds a grading network, which reads all features to predict Gleason patterns and the Grade Group, while morphology maps read directly from the named features. We evaluate the system on five public datasets that include needle biopsies, tissue-microarray cores, multi-reader annotations, and three scanners. The morphology maps remain stable across alignment runs and, without retraining, detect cribriform glands in external biopsies (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUROC, 0.849) and pattern 5 in unseen cores when evaluated by up to six pathologists (AUROC 0.846 to 0.919). In an independent biopsy cohort, Grade Group agreement with three pathologists on Leica scans is close to their agreement with each other. Removing the named features reduces the corresponding Gleason pattern predictions by 49% to 98%, with effects larger than those from 20 activity-matched random feature removals. These results show that a shared sparse representation can support competitive Gleason grading while providing named morphological evidence that transfers across datasets and whose contribution to grading can be measured directly.

AI.tldr: This work builds a prostate biopsy Gleason grading system on a sparse autoencoder over pathology foundation model tokens, aligning 69 of 2048 features with named Gleason morphologies.
AI.motivation: Deep learning systems match pathologists on prostate biopsy grading but typically output a grade without interpretable glandular architecture evidence to justify it.
AI.method: A sparse autoencoder pretrained on biopsies is aligned with multi-reader annotations to name 69 features after morphologies such as cribriform glands, cords, and comedonecrosis, while feeding all features to a grading network and reading morphology maps directly from the named features.
AI.result: Across five public datasets and three scanners, the morphology maps detect cribriform glands in external biopsies (AUROC 0.849) and pattern 5 in unseen cores (AUROC 0.846 to 0.919) without retraining, match inter-pathologist Grade Group agreement on Leica scans, and removing named features drops corresponding pattern predictions by 49% to 98%.
AI.conclusion: A shared sparse representation over foundation model tokens enables competitive Gleason grading alongside transferable, causally measurable morphological explanations.

title: RECLAIM: Robot-Vision-Informed Adversarial Patch Defense via Embodied Attention Feedback
summary: Vision-language-action policies control embodied agents through a perception-action loop grounded in physical interaction, where adversarial patches can corrupt action predictions and thereby alter subsequent observations. To mitigate these threats, many existing defenses rely on policy adaptation or auxiliary models, but require additional training or inference. We introduce RECLAIM, a training-free, inference-time defense that uses a frozen VLA's own attention response to local visual interventions to guide purification during closed-loop embodied manipulation. Our key insight is that attention changes induced by local edits provide feedback for choosing where and how to purify as the robot interacts with its environment. RECLAIM combines this feedback with robot geometry to refine patch localization and select local treatments, then revalidates them as the agent's embodied actions change the observed scene. We evaluate RECLAIM against patches generated by four adversarial attack methods across multiple manipulation task suites under frozen VLA control. Under adversarial patch attacks, RECLAIM succeeds in at least one rollout on 95% of the evaluated tasks and raises rollout success on LIBERO-Object from 0% without defense to 70.0%. Its mean decision time is only 548.9 ms per control step. These results highlight policy-guided visual purification as an effective approach to defending embodied agents against adversarial patches and recovering closed-loop task execution.

AI.tldr: RECLAIM is a training-free, inference-time defense that uses a frozen vision-language-action (VLA) policy's own attention response to local visual edits to detect and purify adversarial patches during closed-loop manipulation.
AI.motivation: Adversarial patches can corrupt VLA action predictions in closed-loop physical interaction, while existing defenses require policy adaptation, auxiliary models, or extra training.
AI.method: RECLAIM combines a frozen VLA's attention changes under local visual interventions with robot geometry to localize patches, select local purification treatments, and revalidate them as the robot's actions alter the scene.
AI.result: Evaluated against four adversarial attack methods across multiple manipulation suites, RECLAIM succeeds in at least one rollout on 95% of tasks, raises LIBERO-Object rollout success from 0% to 70.0%, and runs in 548.9 ms per control step on average.
AI.conclusion: Policy-guided visual purification using embodied attention feedback provides an effective, training-free defense against adversarial patches in closed-loop VLA control.

title: 4D-TEMPO: Differentiable 4D-STEM ptychography via fast Physics Optimizers
comment: 34 pages: 8-page paper, references, and 23-page supplementary material; 10 figures, 10 tables
summary: Electron ptychography recovers atomic structure from 4D-STEM data: diffraction patterns at multiple positions of a scanned probe. Current codes reconstruct an image and read atoms off it, or fit atoms under an $L_1$ loss; neither gives per-atom uncertainty. We propose 4D-TEMPO, a differentiable physical renderer that fits the atoms, the microscope, and the detector directly to the recorded electron counts under a Poisson likelihood. The output is a list of atoms, each a Gaussian primitive with a 3D position, a thermal width, and a model-conditional error bar from the Fisher information. The Fisher information also conditions the solver, gives the dose (electrons per Å$^2$) each parameter needs, and separates calibration from imaging. On a simulated WSe$_2$ bilayer, starting from the published reconstruction, fitted atoms cut in-plane error by a third (3.2 vs. 4.8 pm) and depth error by 40-61% against its 3D peaks. Depth comes from multiple scattering into the dark field, the faint counts outside the direct beam. The two layers, $10\times$ closer than the depth of field, separate; per-atom depth then follows the layer geometry. When the model is well specified, the bars are calibrated (69% of position coordinates within $1\sigma$). On experimental WSe$_2$, fitted atoms predict held-out patterns better than the three published codes we test. With free probe modes where atoms are incomplete, the same likelihood predicts best on all three held-out benchmarks, matches every WSe$_2$ baseline in 5 min against up to 20.5 h, and passes torchslice at its released setting 180$\times$ sooner on PrScO$_3$. Per-atom error bars, planned doses, and fast reconstruction point to low-dose, real-time 3D imaging of beam-sensitive and dynamic materials.

AI.tldr: 4D-TEMPO is a differentiable physical renderer for 4D-STEM electron ptychography that fits atomic Gaussian primitives, microscope, and detector parameters directly to electron counts under a Poisson likelihood.
AI.motivation: Existing 4D-STEM ptychography codes either reconstruct an image before reading off atoms or fit atoms under an L1 loss, providing no per-atom uncertainty estimates.
AI.method: 4D-TEMPO optimizes 3D atomic positions and thermal widths directly against recorded diffraction counts using a Poisson likelihood, while using Fisher information to compute calibrated per-atom error bars, condition the solver, and quantify required electron dose.
AI.result: On simulated WSe2 bilayers, 4D-TEMPO cuts in-plane error by a third (3.2 vs. 4.8 pm) and depth error by 40-61%, calibrates 69% of position coordinates within 1 sigma, and on experimental WSe2 and PrScO3 outperforms three published codes while matching baselines in 5 minutes (up to 20.5 hours) and passing torchslice 180x faster.
AI.conclusion: Direct Poisson-likelihood physical rendering with Fisher information enables fast, dose-aware, uncertainty-calibrated 3D atomic imaging for beam-sensitive materials.

title: $Z$-sight: Unifying Vision-Language-Action and Latent World Modeling
summary: We introduce $Z$-sight, a unified robot foundation model that couples vision-language-action (VLA) and generative latent world modeling. Video-based world action models (WAMs) show the value of joint future-and-action generation for control, yet inherit the heavy cost of video generators. Recent latent-space policies avoid pixel generation, yet typically align intermediate features or rely on frozen target encoders, decoupling future prediction from the VLM's native feature space. $Z$-sight instead predicts the future directly in the visual token space in which its VLM perceives the present. Coupling a foresight expert and a continuous action expert with the VLM in a mixture-of-transformers, $Z$-sight jointly denoises future spatial tokens and actions at inference without pixel reconstruction or external encoders. Trained on human video and robot trajectories, $Z$-sight achieves 81.9% success on SIMPLE (+9.6 points over the strongest baseline) and 73.3% across six Unitree G1 tasks (+20.0 points) at 110 ms per chunk, while remaining competitive on tabletop benchmarks.

AI.tldr: Z-sight is a unified robot foundation model that couples vision-language-action (VLA) control with generative latent world modeling directly in the VLM's native visual token space.
AI.motivation: Video-based world action models incur heavy pixel-generation costs, while recent latent-space policies align intermediate features or rely on frozen target encoders that decouple future prediction from the VLM's native representation.
AI.method: Z-sight integrates a foresight expert and a continuous action expert with a VLM in a mixture-of-transformers architecture, jointly denoising future spatial tokens and actions at inference without pixel reconstruction or external encoders.
AI.result: Trained on human video and robot trajectories, Z-sight achieves 81.9% success on SIMPLE (+9.6 points over the strongest baseline) and 73.3% across six Unitree G1 tasks (+20.0 points) at 110 ms per chunk, while remaining competitive on tabletop benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Jointly denoising future visual tokens and actions within the VLM's native token space delivers strong manipulation performance at low inference latency.

title: VisHintPrompt : A Visual Hint Prompting Strategy for Numerical Inference from Charts

AI.tldr: The paper proposes VisHintPrompt, a scaffolded visual hint prompting strategy that improves numerical inference from both Cartesian and polar charts in pretrained Multimodal Large Language Models without additional training.
AI.motivation: Chart-specific models struggle to generalize beyond the chart types and visual encodings in their training data, while reliable visual prompting methods to elicit fine-grained numerical inference from pretrained MLLMs remain largely unexplored.
AI.method: VisHintPrompt extracts coordinate priors and progressively narrows the search region using three components: Coordinate-aware Grid Enhancement to overlay structure-aligned grids, Iterative Visual Feedback to overlay alignment cues from intermediate predictions, and Progressive Zoom-in Refinement to enlarge regions of interest with denser grids.
AI.result: Experiments across diverse Cartesian (e.g., bar, scatterplot) and polar (e.g., pie, radar) charts on proprietary and open-source MLLMs show improvements over standard prompting, with ablation studies confirming the complementary roles of each component.
AI.conclusion: Structured, visual-centric prompting grounded in coordinate priors enables reliable and more accurate quantitative chart interpretation in general-purpose MLLMs without task-specific retraining.

title: Splats in Splats++: Robust and Generalizable 3D Gaussian Splatting Steganography

AI.tldr: Splats in Splats++ is a pipeline-agnostic steganography framework that embeds high-capacity 3D and 4D content directly into native 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) representations.
AI.motivation: Existing invisible embedding methods for 3DGS assets struggle to balance high-capacity, attack-resilient hiding with asset utility, often disrupting the native rendering pipeline or leaking messages under structural perturbations.
AI.method: The framework uses an importance-graded Spherical Harmonics coefficient encryption scheme, a Hash-Grid Guided Opacity Mapping mechanism, and a Gradient-Gated Opacity Consistency Loss to couple original and hidden scenes in a continuous, attack-resilient latent manifold.
AI.result: Experiments show up to 6.28 dB higher message fidelity, 3x faster rendering, robustness against 3D structural attacks such as GSPure, and generalization to 2D image embedding and 4D dynamic scene steganography.
AI.conclusion: Principled Spherical Harmonics encryption and continuous opacity-consistency coupling enable robust, high-capacity copyright protection within native 3DGS assets.

title: Real-World Spectral Compressive Imaging by Learning a Physics-Informed Forward Model

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a learnable physics-informed forward model (LPFM) and the real-world rSCI dataset to bridge the simulation-to-reality gap in coded aperture snapshot spectral imaging (CASSI) reconstruction.
AI.motivation: Learning-based CASSI reconstruction methods perform well on simulated data but degrade significantly on real systems due to a mismatch between idealized simulations and the complex real imaging process.
AI.method: The authors propose LPFM, which embeds the physical structure of CASSI into a learnable proxy network to model the real imaging process, and construct rSCI, a dataset of 219 static HSI-CASSI image pairs across indoor and outdoor scenes plus dynamic CASSI videos.
AI.result: Using rSCI and LPFM to establish the first real-world CASSI reconstruction benchmark, experiments show that training with LPFM-generated data reduces the simulation-to-reality gap and consistently improves reconstruction across various state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: Combining a physics-informed learnable forward model with paired real-world measurements provides an effective foundation for advancing practical hyperspectral snapshot imaging reconstruction.

title: Bridging the Thermal Gap: Data-Model Collaborative Transfer for Infrared Perception

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a data-model collaborative transfer framework that jointly optimizes training data generation and infrared-specific model adaptation for infrared visual perception.
AI.motivation: Existing infrared perception methods decouple data construction from model transfer, ignoring their interdependence and failing to explicitly model infrared-specific thermal imaging characteristics.
AI.method: A task-responsive generator learns weights over a feasible infrared imaging-variation space to build informative training observations, while a formation-guided representation module extracts radiance-structure and response-detail descriptors that a thermal-aware adapter uses to modulate intermediate features via residual corrections under a single-loop training strategy.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on image enhancement, depth estimation, small-target detection, and semantic segmentation show consistent improvements across multiple foundation-model backbones with a small trainable parameter budget.
AI.conclusion: Coordinating data generation, physical representation learning, and lightweight adapter optimization in a single loop enables effective and parameter-efficient transfer for infrared visual perception.

title: Knowledge-enhanced Incomplete Multi-view Clustering on Relational Knowledge

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a knowledge-enhanced anchor-based incomplete multi-view clustering (IMVC) framework for relational knowledge and constructs 45 benchmark datasets across varying missing ratios.
AI.motivation: Traditional intra-view and inter-view imputation strategies rely on observed features that can introduce semantic noise and bias, and they fail to sufficiently utilize structural knowledge in relational knowledge multi-view clustering.
AI.method: The authors introduce an anchor-based IMVC framework incorporating two structural knowledge enhancement mechanisms: one applied to anchors and the other to the anchor graph.
AI.result: Evaluated against 10 baseline models across 45 newly constructed incomplete multi-view datasets with missing ratios from 10% to 90%, the method demonstrates strong performance across superiority, stability, sensitivity, complexity, and visualization.
AI.conclusion: Enhancing anchors and anchor graphs with structural knowledge improves expressive ability for relational knowledge IMVC, and the 45 constructed datasets provide a benchmark for future research.

title: Human–AI Divergence in Ego-Centric Action Recognition Under Spatial and Spatiotemporal Manipulations

AI.tldr: This large-scale human-AI study compares over 3,000 human participants with Side4Video and Qwen 3.5 9B on egocentric action recognition under spatial reduction and temporal scrambling.
AI.motivation: Humans outperform AI models in degraded real-world action recognition, and understanding the mechanisms behind this gap is needed to build more human-aligned models.
AI.method: Using the Epic-ReduAct dataset derived from 36 EPIC-KITCHENS videos, the authors evaluate human-defined Minimal Identifiable Recognition Crops (MIRCs) alongside spatial reduction and temporal scrambling, analyzing Average Reduction Rate, Recognition Gap, and Low vs. High Temporal Actions.
AI.result: Human accuracy drops sharply from MIRCs to sub-MIRCs due to reliance on sparse hand-object cues, whereas models degrade gradually using contextual low-level features (sometimes with higher confidence), and humans resist temporal scrambling when spatial cues remain while models show class-dependent insensitivity.
AI.conclusion: Strong standard benchmark scores can mask fundamental human-AI misalignment in how spatial and temporal cues are used for action recognition.

title: UniE2F: A Unified Diffusion Framework for Event-to-Frame Reconstruction with Video Foundation Models

AI.tldr: UniE2F is a unified diffusion framework that leverages a pre-trained video diffusion model to reconstruct high-fidelity video frames from sparse event camera data and perform zero-shot interpolation and prediction.
AI.motivation: Event cameras capture relative intensity changes with high speed and dynamic range, but lack spatial information and static texture details needed for full-frame video reconstruction.
AI.method: UniE2F conditions a pre-trained video diffusion model on event streams, adds event-based inter-frame residual guidance grounded in physical event-frame correlations, and modulates reverse diffusion sampling for zero-shot frame interpolation and prediction.
AI.result: On real-world and synthetic datasets, UniE2F outperforms prior event-to-frame reconstruction methods on most quantitative metrics and qualitative comparisons, and matches dedicated trained methods in zero-shot interpolation and prediction.
AI.conclusion: Combining video diffusion priors with physics-grounded event residual guidance unifies event-to-frame reconstruction, interpolation, and prediction.

title: FLAME: Flow Guidance and Adaptive Frequency Fusion for All-in-One Mamba-Enhanced Video Restoration

AI.tldr: The paper proposes FLAME, an all-in-one video restoration framework that combines explicit flow-guided alignment with implicit Mamba sequence modeling and adaptive frequency fusion for adverse weather degradations.
AI.motivation: Existing all-in-one video restoration methods either rely on explicit optical flow that fails under heavy weather degradations or use implicit sequence modeling that lacks fine-grained temporal correspondence.
AI.method: FLAME integrates three components: Dual-Path Mamba Modeling with Space-Time Sequence and Hilbert-Sequence Mamba blocks, Flow-guided Lightweight Attention with degradation-aware flow estimation and deformable fusion, and Adaptive Frequency Residual Fusion with learnable frequency decomposition and cross-channel attention.
AI.result: FLAME achieves state-of-the-art results, reaching 35.50 dB PSNR on VRDS (+3.46 dB over RainMamba), 40.17 dB on LWDDS (+2.96 dB over RainMamba), 31.04 dB on W3 (+0.59 dB over AIM-VR), and 29.00 dB on RainSynAll100 (+1.33 dB over BasicVSR++).
AI.conclusion: Synergizing explicit degradation-aware flow alignment with implicit linear-complexity Mamba modeling and frequency fusion effectively restores videos across diverse adverse weather conditions.

title: Object recognition from dynamic cues: Examining the inversion effect

AI.tldr: This study uses object kinematograms to show that turning dynamic-only visual stimuli upside down impairs human object recognition, with effects varying by category.
AI.motivation: While inversion effects are well documented for static images and human action videos, it was unknown whether inversion impairs recognition across broader object categories when only dynamic motion cues are available.
AI.method: Motion cues extracted from videos of four animate and four inanimate categories were projected onto randomly moving dots (object kinematograms), and online participants performed animacy judgment, subordinate categorization, and object naming on upright and inverted stimuli.
AI.result: Inversion impaired motion-based object categorization overall, with a small effect for animate (and none significant for inanimate) animacy judgments, and significant inversion effects in several animate and inanimate categories for subordinate categorization and naming.
AI.conclusion: Orientation-dependent processing extends to dynamic-only object recognition, likely reflecting natural orientation statistics or physical motion dynamics.

title: Sequential biases in the perception of proportion

AI.tldr: Three behavioral experiments demonstrate systematic sequential biases in human judgments of both numerosity-based and area-based visual proportions.
AI.motivation: Although history effects are established for many visual features, whether and how sequential biases emerge in proportion perception remained unclear.
AI.method: Participants completed two-alternative forced-choice proportion judgments across three experiments: numerosity proportions manipulated by brightness (Experiment 1) or shape (Experiment 2), and area ratios between two objects with constant total area (Experiment 3).
AI.result: All three experiments showed systematic sequential biases that decayed over time: brightness-based numerosity and area-ratio judgments exhibited repulsive biases away from the prior trial's proportion, whereas shape-based numerosity judgments exhibited an attractive bias.
AI.conclusion: Proportion perception is shaped by prior trial history through distinct mechanisms such as sensory adaptation or serial dependence depending on the visual cue.

title: Online Quantum State Tomography via Stochastic Gradient Descent

AI.tldr: This paper proposes non-convex mini-batch stochastic gradient descent (SGD) algorithms for online quantum state tomography (QST) and proves their local geometric convergence.
AI.motivation: Online QST requires sequentially updating a low-rank quantum state estimate from streaming batch measurements without storing past observables or outcomes.
AI.method: Building on non-convex low-rank QST optimization, the authors design memory-efficient mini-batch SGD algorithms that update the state matrix using only current-round measurement outcomes and observables.
AI.result: With proper initialization, the squared error contracts locally in conditional expectation to a finite-shot noise floor with high-probability geometric convergence, achieving nearly optimal sample complexity and better time complexity in rank and log-dimension than state-of-the-art non-convex QST methods.
AI.conclusion: Non-convex mini-batch SGD provides a theoretically grounded, memory- and time-efficient approach for practical online quantum state tomography.

title: When Does Window Position Matter in Protein Language Models? A Controlled Benchmark and Cross-Architecture Taxonomy

AI.tldr: A controlled benchmark across eight protein language models shows that window-position effects arise from one-sided loss of informative context rather than position encodings themselves.
AI.motivation: Protein language models process long sequences in fixed-length windows, but it was unclear whether, why, and when a residue's position within a window alters model behavior.
AI.method: Using content-controlled probes across seven bidirectional encoders (including ESM-2, ESM-1b, ESM C, SaProt, ProtT5, Ankh, ProtBERT) and one causal model (ProGen2), the authors isolate five candidate mechanisms and evaluate representations, variant effects, secondary structure, and long-range contacts.
AI.result: Bidirectional encoders show a modest center-favored inverted-U in representation similarity that disappears when context is held fixed and is absent in randomly initialized models; cutting context beyond a contact partner drops confident contact probability by 20 points, while centering on the domain recovers 98% of edge representation loss.
AI.conclusion: Window position matters specifically when window boundaries sever informative local or contact context, and overlapping or domain-centered windows mitigate most of the degradation.

title: Heat and Matérn Kernels on Matchings

AI.tldr: This paper develops stationary heat and Matérn kernels on the discrete space of matchings and introduces a sub-exponential zonal-polynomial algorithm for evaluating them.
AI.motivation: Applying kernel methods to matchings is hindered by their non-Euclidean geometry and the prohibitive super-exponential cost of naively evaluating stationary kernels.
AI.method: The authors characterize all stationary kernels on matchings, formulate heat and Matérn kernel families with smoothness inductive bias, design a sub-exponential evaluation algorithm using zonal polynomials, and test transferring the framework to phylogenetic trees via their bijection with matchings.
AI.result: The zonal-polynomial algorithm reduces kernel evaluation from super-exponential to sub-exponential complexity, while transferring the framework to phylogenetic trees yields novel negative results and identifies an open problem.
AI.conclusion: Stationary heat and Matérn kernels with sub-exponential evaluation establish theoretical and computational foundations for kernel methods on matchings.

title: Cascading Bandits: Minimizing Regret with Respect to the Optimal Ordering

AI.tldr: This paper studies cascading bandits where the learner minimizes the cumulative number of arm pulls to reach a success, proposing O-UCB and O-Greedy with O(log T) and O(1) regret bounds.
AI.motivation: In applications like cognitive radios and carousel recommendations, arms are pulled sequentially until the first success, making pull-count minimization relative to the optimal ordering the key objective.
AI.method: The authors define regret as expected extra pulls compared to the optimal arm ordering and adapt UCB and Greedy into two algorithms, O-UCB and O-Greedy.
AI.result: O-UCB achieves both an O(log T) gap-dependent regret bound and an O(1) bound depending on an inherent-exploration parameter p_all, while O-Greedy also achieves O(1) regret under the same conditions, as corroborated by synthetic and semi-synthetic experiments.
AI.conclusion: Inherent exploration in sequential-until-success cascading bandits enables even greedy ordering strategies to achieve constant regret.

title: From Keypoints to Predictive Distributions: Post-Hoc Uncertainty for YOLO-Pose Models

AI.tldr: This work adds lightweight post-hoc probabilistic heads to trained YOLO-Pose models to output calibrated bivariate Gaussian or Student-t predictive distributions over keypoint locations.
AI.motivation: YOLO-Pose models localize multi-object keypoints efficiently but do not quantify spatial uncertainty for downstream reliability ranking or sensor fusion.
AI.method: Using importance-weighted negative log-likelihood, additional heads predict an input-dependent 2x2 dispersion matrix per keypoint followed by Gaussian or Student-t calibration, evaluated with distributional calibration diagnostics and average keypoint precision (AKP).
AI.result: On COCO with YOLO-NAS-Pose and YOLO26-Pose, the learned uncertainties enable keypoint reliability ranking and pruning of unreliable keypoints, with Student-t calibration best matching empirical residuals, and support uncertainty-aware position estimation in aircraft landing.
AI.conclusion: Post-hoc dispersion heads with Student-t calibration provide practical, calibrated spatial uncertainty for real-time YOLO-Pose keypoint detectors.

title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models: Phenomenology, Mechanism, and Recipe

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the mechanisms of on-policy distillation (OPD) in LLMs, identifying two failure conditions and showing that successful OPD aligns high-probability tokens at student-visited states.
AI.motivation: On-policy distillation is widely used in LLM post-training, yet its training dynamics and the reasons it succeeds or fails remain poorly understood.
AI.method: The authors analyze OPD through weak-to-strong reverse distillation (1.5B and 7B teachers), token-level probability probing, and two recovery strategies: off-policy cold start and teacher-aligned prompt selection.
AI.result: OPD requires compatible student-teacher thinking patterns and genuinely new teacher capabilities; successful OPD progressively aligns a small shared token set holding 97% to 99% of probability mass at student-visited states, while dense token-level rewards incur costs for long-horizon scaling.
AI.conclusion: Understanding OPD's dependence on thinking-pattern compatibility and shared high-probability token alignment enables targeted recovery strategies when distillation stalls.

title: Vera: A Layered Diffusion Model for Content-Preserving Video Editing

AI.tldr: Vera is a layered video diffusion framework that generates an edit layer and alpha matte separately from the source video to preserve unchanged content during video editing.
AI.motivation: Existing video diffusion editors regenerate every pixel, frequently altering characters or backgrounds that should remain untouched.
AI.method: Vera extends a text-to-video DiT into a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) with separate DiTs per layer interacting via joint self-attention, trained on a newly constructed 486K-frame layered dataset with accurate alpha mattes.
AI.result: Across quantitative benchmarks and a human preference study, Vera outperforms leading open-source video editing models in content preservation while maintaining competitive edit quality.
AI.conclusion: Separating creative edits and alpha mattes from the source video via Mixture-of-Transformers layers enables high-fidelity, content-preserving video editing.

title: FuseSR+: Spatial-Temporal Fusion for High-Scale Super-Resolution

AI.tldr: FuseSR+ is a real-time neural super-resolution method that fuses non-aligned spatial and temporal features with high-resolution auxiliary G-buffers to achieve stable 4x4 and 8x8 upsampling at 4K resolution.
AI.motivation: Real-time rendering workloads are growing rapidly, and existing super-resolution methods rely primarily on low-resolution temporal information that is too sparse to recover fine details for high-scale upsampling.
AI.method: The method introduces low-cost historical and current high-resolution auxiliary G-buffers alongside an H-Net architecture, pixel shuffling and unshuffling layers to align low- and high-resolution features, and a lightweight temporal feature recurrent module to aggregate high-resolution temporal features.
AI.result: Experiments on 4x4 and 8x8 upsampling tasks at 4K resolution show that FuseSR+ achieves real-time performance with temporally consistent reconstructions, improved visual quality, significant performance gains, and better temporal stability than existing methods.
AI.conclusion: Combining non-aligned spatial-temporal features with high-resolution auxiliary G-buffers enables stable, high-scale real-time super-resolution without noticeable quality loss.

title: A Survey of Post-Training in Time Series Foundation Models

AI.tldr: This survey categorizes post-training methods for time series foundation models (TSFMs) by their intervention locus in the prediction pipeline and outlines future research directions for reliable downstream deployment.
AI.motivation: Pretraining alone is often insufficient for deploying TSFMs reliably due to domain shift, task heterogeneity, limited supervision, and computational constraints, necessitating a structured understanding of post-training interventions.
AI.method: The authors analyze TSFM post-training methods by where they intervene in the prediction pipeline, organizing them into five categories: parameter adaptation, context augmentation, model composition, output processing and uncertainty control, and compression and specialization.
AI.result: The survey examines representative methods and current limitations within each of the five categories and identifies future directions including controlled adaptation, reliable context construction, uncertainty-aware model composition, calibrated output processing, and deployment-aware specialization.
AI.conclusion: By establishing a unifying framework for the TSFM post-training landscape, the survey helps researchers navigate the design space between pretrained models and reliable downstream deployment.

title: Differentiable Numerical Association Rule Learning

AI.tldr: DiffNARM is a differentiable unsupervised method for numerical association rule mining (NARM) that jointly learns globally shared feature bins and association rules end-to-end, achieving strong rule quality with fewer rules and faster scaling than heuristic approaches.
AI.motivation: Existing NARM methods rely on rule-level population-based heuristic search that cannot scale to large datasets or produce globally shared bins, or on pre-discretization independent of rule quality that causes information loss.
AI.method: DiffNARM uses a soft binning module to generate differentiable bin membership vectors, mitigates boundary collapse in differentiable binning, and jointly learns associations across both numerical and categorical features end-to-end.
AI.result: On real-world datasets, DiffNARM achieves comparable rule quality with up to 8 times fewer rules than exhaustive miners, generalizes to unseen data with under 0.5% loss in confidence and association strength, and runs one to two orders of magnitude faster than population-based heuristic search methods.
AI.conclusion: Differentiable end-to-end learning of shared bin structures and association rules overcomes the scalability and information-loss bottlenecks of traditional NARM techniques.

title: CaRT: Teaching LLM Agents to Know When They Know Enough

AI.tldr: Counterfactuals and Reasoning for Termination (CaRT) teaches LLM agents when to stop gathering information and act by fine-tuning on counterfactual trajectory pairs with verbal termination rationales.
AI.motivation: Strategic multi-round information gathering requires LLM agents to know not only how to acquire information but also when to stop so they do not overthink or get derailed before acting.
AI.method: CaRT formalizes the termination problem and fine-tunes LLMs on counterfactual pairs of trajectories, one where termination is appropriate and a modified version where it is not, training the model to explain the termination rationale via verbal reasoning.
AI.result: Instantiated in interactive medical diagnosis and math problem solving, CaRT improves both information-gathering efficiency and task success rate compared to other fine-tuning methods.
AI.conclusion: Training LLMs with counterfactual trajectory pairs and verbalized termination reasoning effectively teaches agents when they have enough information to act.
